accuracy.evidence: Checked against NASA Solar System Exploration 'Sun: facts' (G-type main-sequence star, about 150 million km, sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds), NASA/ESA pages on Proxima Centauri (4.24 light years, about 0.15 solar radii) and Sirius (8.6 light years, Sirius A about 1.7 solar radii), and Joyce et al. 2020 ApJ 902:63 for Betelgeuse (about 750 solar radii; distance about 550 light years with wide uncertainty, so the lesson says only 'hundreds of times wider' and 'hundreds of years'). The National Curriculum Year 5 Earth and space statements are quoted exactly. Venus as the 'evening star' and the Moon and planets shining by reflected sunlight match the Royal Museums Greenwich guidance.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets misconceptions documented in Sharp (1996) 'Children's astronomical beliefs' (Research in Science Education 26) and Vosniadou and Brewer (1994) on children's models of the day/night cycle: the Sun is not a star ('planet', 'tiny', prediction 1, m2), the Sun is the biggest star ('biggest', prediction 2, m6), the Sun orbits the Earth ('earth', prediction 4, m8), the Moon makes its own light ('glow', prediction 3, m4), Venus is a star ('venus', m3) and stars vanish in daytime ('gone', m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstar is about the Sun as a nearby star: a distance slider shrinks the Sun to a point among a fixed star field, a real-size view compares Proxima Centauri, Sirius and Betelgeuse with the Sun, a sort separates light sources from reflectors, a drag puts the Sun at the centre before a year runs, and light pulses time the trip from three stars. flagpname orders planet names, flagsky does day/night/seasons for ages 4-5 and flagsun is sunlight heating. Max 6-shingle similarity 3.3% (flag_regpol.js); explanation overlap 0.1%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the key idea before being told it: flying away makes the Sun shrink to the same dot as the field stars and only then is it labelled; switching to real sizes shows Sirius larger than the Sun and Betelgeuse too big to fit; the Moon and Venus land in 'reflects light' with the reason; the Earth cannot orbit until the Sun is dragged to the middle; the light pulses take visibly longer from the other stars, with 8 minutes against 4 and 8.5 years.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'still a big yellow ball' (it shrinks to a dot), 'yes, it looks the biggest' (real sizes show bigger stars), 'yes, it shines' for the Moon (sorting shows it reflects sunlight), and 'the Earth' at the centre (the starting scene has Earth in the middle and the learner must move the Sun there).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions with nine distinct feedback messages that name the slip: 'Planets do not make light...' for calling the Sun a planet, 'Stars look tiny only because they are so far away', 'Many stars are bigger. Betelgeuse is hundreds of times wider', 'It looks as if the Sun moves across our sky, but the Earth goes round the Sun', 'Venus is called the evening star, but it is a planet', 'The bright daytime sky hides their faint light', 'All 8 planets orbit the Sun'.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short, concrete sentences for ages 7-9 with the target terms star, Sun, solar system, planet, orbit, reflect, light; validate_lessons passes the kid and adult readability limits. Lab step text is one or two sentences; star facts use 'just over 4 years' and 'almost twice as wide' rather than raw numbers. Adult text lists key vocabulary and the Year 5 statements.

no_filler.evidence: Gate finds no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph teaches one point (what a star is; near looks big; Sun at the centre; reflected light). Items avoid recall-by-copying: m7 compares light-travel times to judge distance, p5 multiplies the 8-minute trip, m9 counts the other planets. Every hint points to the reasoning, every explanation gives the reason.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: star labels at 10-12 px on light cards are readable against the dark space background; the distance slider knob is 14 px radius with the lower quarter of the canvas as its drag area; sorting boxes and the three light rows are tall tap targets; solar-system orbits fit the canvas; control buttons wrap to two or three rows with nothing clipped. Desktop 1200 px also checked.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: Fly farther / Come closer, Real sizes toggle plus a button per star, Makes its own light / Reflects light, Put the Sun in the middle / Run a year, and Light from each star. The canvas aria-label is updated with each result, the challenge feedback is a polite live region, and walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
